## Purpose and Runtime

TG-FileStreamBot is a Go service that turns Telegram-hosted files into direct HTTP streaming/download links. It combines a Telegram bot interface with an HTTP server and a Telegram user-session client used to retrieve file bytes.

Primary executable: `cmd/fsb/main.go`. Process startup, bot/session initialization, and service orchestration are organized in `cmd/fsb/run.go` and `cmd/fsb/session.go`.

## Bootstrap and Configuration

`cmd/fsb/main.go` launches the application; `cmd/fsb/run.go` composes the major subsystems. `config/config.go` is the central configuration boundary, likely sourcing bot credentials, Telegram API/session settings, server configuration, and cache behavior from environment variables.

Deployment targets include containerized and process-platform environments via `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yaml`, and `Procfile`.

## Telegram Interaction Layer

The Telegram-facing application is implemented in `internal/bot/userbot.go`, `internal/bot/client.go`, and `internal/bot/middleware.go`. This layer owns Telegram client connectivity, incoming update handling, and cross-cutting bot validation/error behavior.

Command dispatch lives in `internal/commands/commands.go`. User-facing workflows include startup/onboarding in `internal/commands/start.go` and generation of stream links from Telegram messages/files in `internal/commands/stream.go`.

## File-Link and Response Flow

A user submits or references a Telegram file through the bot. The command layer resolves file metadata and produces a stream-link response using shared models in `internal/types/file.go` and `internal/types/response.go`.

Link generation and file-access identity depend on utility functions such as hashing in `internal/utils/hashing.go`. This separates externally exposed stream identifiers from Telegram’s underlying file references.

## HTTP Routing and Stream Delivery

The public HTTP boundary is defined by `internal/routes/routes.go`, with stream-specific endpoint handling in `internal/routes/stream.go`. These handlers accept a generated link/request, resolve the corresponding Telegram file, and return an HTTP response suitable for browser/media-client consumption.

Actual transfer is handled by `internal/stream/pipe.go`; stream failures are modeled in `internal/stream/errors.go`. This is the key protocol boundary: HTTP request/response semantics on one side, Telegram file retrieval on the other.

## Session, Caching, and Background Work

Telegram user authorization/session lifecycle is coordinated from `cmd/fsb/session.go`; QR-login support is packaged in `pkg/qrlogin/qrcode.go` and `pkg/qrlogin/encoder.go`. This supports authenticated Telegram file access independently of the bot command channel.

`internal/cache/cache.go` provides a state/cache boundary for reusable file or link-related data. `internal/bot/workers.go` contains asynchronous/background bot work, keeping long-running or deferred tasks outside the immediate update handler path.

## External Dependencies and Operational Boundaries

The system integrates with Telegram through bot and user-client APIs, including the credited `gotgproto` ecosystem. Telegram is the authoritative file source; the service exposes the derived HTTP streaming surface. Runtime observability/logging utilities are centralized in `internal/utils/logger.go`, while releases are built and packaged through `.goreleaser.yaml` and GitHub release automation.
